sections.h2: Where is Brockton, Massachusetts, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Brockton is a city in Plymouth County, about 22 miles south of Boston and 30 miles northeast of Providence. The 2020 census counted 105,643 residents, which makes it the sixth-largest city in Massachusetts and the most populous community in the county.

It covers 21.5 square miles of land. Avon, Holbrook, Abington, Whitman, East Bridgewater, West Bridgewater, Easton and Stoughton border it. Brockton and Plymouth share the role of county seat.

Most of the city is built up. The Salisbury Plain River once powered the shoe factories, and the largest green space is D.W. Field Park, an Olmsted-inspired park with ponds and a golf course. The city uses ZIP codes 02301 through 02305.

sections.h2: What is Brockton's history, and why does it matter for old houses?
sections.html:
Brockton was part of Bridgewater until June 15, 1821, when it was set off as North Bridgewater. Residents voted to rename it Brockton on May 5, 1874, and it became a city on April 9, 1881.

Shoes built the housing stock. Wikipedia reports that Brockton was the country's largest shoe producer during the Civil War, and the shoe industry stayed large until late in the twentieth century. W.B. Mason, the office supply company, has been headquartered here since 1898.

On October 1, 1883, Thomas Edison switched on the first three-wire underground electrical system in the world in Brockton. In 1896 it became the first city in the country to abolish grade crossings.

Brockton is often described through its villages and wards rather than one downtown. Montello and Campello are two villages with their own MBTA commuter rail stations and post offices. Campello is the smallest by area and the most populous.

  • West Brockton uses ZIP code 02301, East Brockton uses 02302.
  • Downtown runs along Main Street, and City Hall is at 45 School Street.
  • The South Street Historic District and D.W. Field Park are listed among the city's notable places.
  • The city council has seven ward councilors and four councilors at large.

If you are selling, tell a buyer which village or ward the house is in. Those three villages have rail stations.

Wikipedia also notes that Brockton became the first city in New England with a majority-Black population in 2020, and that about 16 percent of residents are of Cape Verdean ancestry according to the 2023 American Community Survey five-year estimates. The city holds a Cape Verdean Festival on the last Sunday in July.

sections.h2: What jobs and institutions anchor Brockton's economy?
sections.html:
The shoe economy has given way to health care, education and manufacturing. Brockton has three hospitals: Signature Healthcare Brockton Hospital on the east side, Boston Medical Center South in the northwest and the Brockton VA Hospital in the southwest.

  • Massasoit Community College is based in the city, and Fisher College and Eastern Nazarene College have campuses here as well.
  • W.B. Mason has its headquarters in Brockton.
  • The Brockton Rox play professional baseball at Campanelli Stadium.
  • Brockton Area Transit runs the local buses.

sections.h2: How do you get around Brockton?
sections.html:
Route 24 is a six-lane highway on the west side of the city with exits at Route 27 to the north and Route 123 to the south. Those two routes cross at the center of the city, and Route 28 runs north to south through the middle.

The MBTA Fall River/New Bedford Line stops at Montello, Brockton and Campello. Brockton Area Transit buses also connect to Ashmont Station, Stoughton, the Bridgewater Industrial Park and Braintree Station via a stop in Montello.

That transit map is worth using in your listing or your talk with a buyer. A house within a short walk of a commuter rail station reaches Boston without a car.

sections.h2: What is Brockton's weather like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Brockton gets about 50 inches of precipitation and about 34 inches of snow in a typical year, based on NOAA 1991 to 2020 normals reproduced on Wikipedia. January daily highs average near 39 degrees and July highs near 84 degrees.

The record high is 105 degrees and the record low is minus 19. Wikipedia also calls Brockton one of the windiest cities in the country, with wind speeds averaging 14.3 miles per hour. Wind and snow are the load a roof carries here.

Ice, wind and the freeze and thaw cycle test older roofs, chimneys, gutters and foundation walls. A buyer's inspector will check those items, so a roof quote or a chimney report can help you in a negotiation.

sections.h2: How do Brockton property tax bills and abatements work?
sections.html:
Brockton issues four bills a year. The first two, on July 1 and October 1, are preliminary and based on last year's taxes. The third, issued January 1, is the actual bill with the new rate. The fourth is issued April 1.

Each bill is due within 30 days of its issue date. The Board of Assessors says an abatement application must be filed by February 1, or postmarked by that date, and exemptions and deferrals are due within 90 days of the actual bill. The office is at City Hall, 45 School Street, and the phone is 508-580-7194.

The assessors also review deed recordings from the Plymouth County Registry of Deeds and building permits, then update the property's value. After you sell, expect the record to change. Details are on the city's assessors page.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Brockton need to do before closing?
sections.html:
The Massachusetts deed excise tax is $2.00 per $500 of price under MGL c. 64D, s. 1, and it is paid when the deed is recorded. The Department of Fire Services also requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the standard for sale. Call the fire department as soon as you have a closing date, because it charges a fee for the inspection.

  • Gather the deed and your latest tax bill.
  • Note which alarms are older than ten years and replace them.
  • Collect permit records for work done in recent years.
  • For a two- or three-family, gather leases and rent rolls.

If you want a quick sale without repairs, Cash Home Buyers will look at a Brockton house as is. You can compare that with the cost and time of listing.

sections.h2: Why do some Brockton owners choose a cash sale over listing?
sections.html:
Owners choose a cash sale when time, condition or paperwork makes a listing hard. Common cases include an inherited house, a house with tenants, deferred repairs, a move on a short deadline or back taxes.

Brockton's tax calendar is a useful reference point. Bills arrive four times a year, so a missed payment can build up quickly. If you owe taxes, ask the collector's office what the balance is and raise it with your closing attorney before you set a price.

A listing still makes sense for a house in good condition with time on your side. We are not the right fit for every seller, and a cash offer is a choice you can compare with an agent's estimate. Ask for any offer in writing and read the numbers before you decide.

faqs.q: What is Brockton, MA known for?
faqs.a: Brockton is known as the City of Champions because boxers Rocky Marciano and Marvin Hagler came from there. It was also a leading shoe manufacturing city and the site of the first three-wire underground electrical system in the world.
Brockton is in Plymouth County. It is one of the county's two seats, along with Plymouth.

faqs.q: Does Brockton offer a residential exemption?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Assessors states that Brockton does not offer the residential exemption.

faqs.q: When are Brockton property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Each of the four quarterly bills is due within 30 days of its issue date. They are issued July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a property tax abatement in Brockton?
faqs.a: The abatement application must reach the Assessor's Office, or be postmarked, by February 1. If February 1 falls on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Brockton?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for a home sale or transfer. Schedule the inspection once you have a closing date.
